customer_name: Suzhou Botian Automation Technology Co., Ltd. (苏州博田自动化技术有限公司)
business_problem: Suzhou Botian needed a robust way to guide tractors and agricultural robots through non-structured rice-field environments where lighting changes, floating plants, missing seedlings, and reflections made traditional image-processing methods too unreliable for precise automated navigation.
solution_summary: Suzhou Botian used PaddlePaddle, PaddleSeg, and the BML full-featured AI development platform to build an automatic rice-field navigation-line detection system for agricultural machinery. The workflow starts with image collection across different transplanting stages, times of day, and exposure settings so the model can handle varied brightness and field conditions. Botian then uses the ICNet segmentation model from PaddleSeg to separate seedling rows from the background, extract the outer contour and feature points, and identify the center lines of the middle rows that guide navigation. Training is managed through configurable hyperparameters, image augmentation, and VisualDL-based validation, allowing the team to pick the best model without overfitting. Once deployed, the vision module is paired with GPS so agricultural robots can navigate autonomously from leaving storage through returning after work.

solution_components.name: PaddlePaddle
solution_components.role: Provides the deep-learning framework used to train the rice-field navigation model.

solution_components.name: PaddleSeg
solution_components.role: Supplies the segmentation toolkit and ICNet model used to isolate seedling rows and extract navigation lines.

solution_components.name: BML Full-Featured AI Development Platform
solution_components.role: Supports model-development and deployment workflows for the agricultural vision system.

data_flow: Field images collected under different transplanting stages and lighting conditions enter the segmentation workflow, where PaddleSeg isolates seedlings from the background and extracts navigation center lines. Those outputs are combined with GPS and fed into agricultural robots so they can steer automatically across the rice field.
business_outcome: Suzhou Botian improved the precision and speed of agricultural-machine vision navigation, reduced manual labor requirements, and created a reusable perception foundation for broader intelligent-agriculture robotics.
metrics: Per-frame processing time was about 300 ms.
Average angle error dropped from 3.27° to 1.65°.
Large angle errors above 5° were largely avoided even under reflections and missing plants.
architecture_clues: The training set included 400 images for each of two transplanting stages captured across different times of day and exposure settings
ICNet was selected because it balanced low memory use, real-time inference, and acceptable accuracy for embedded deployment
The final deployment combines the visual detector with GPS for end-to-end autonomous navigation
